verses.1:1: In many parts and in many ways, God, having spoken long ago to the fathers in the prophets,
verses.1:2: at the end of these days spoke to us in a Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages;
verses.1:3: who, being the radiance of the glory and the exact impress of His essence, and sustaining all things by the word of His power, having made purification for sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
verses.1:4: having become so much superior to the angels, to the extent that He has inherited a more distinguished name than they.
verses.1:5: For to which of the angels has He ever said, "You are My Son; today I have fathered You," and again, "I will be to Him a Father, and He will be to Me a Son"?
verses.1:6: And when He again brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, He says, "And let all the angels of God worship Him."
verses.1:7: And regarding the angels He says, "He who makes His angels winds, and His ministers a flame of fire,"
verses.1:8: but regarding the Son, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of His kingdom.
verses.1:9: You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, Your God, anointed You with the oil of gladness beyond Your companions."
verses.1:10: And, "You, in the beginning, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the works of Your hands;
verses.1:11: they will perish, but You remain; and they will all grow old like a garment,
verses.1:12: and like a cloak You will roll them up, like a garment they will also be changed; but You are the same, and Your years will not fail."
verses.1:13: But to which of the angels has He ever said, "Sit at My right hand until I place Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet"?
verses.1:14: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent out for service for the sake of those who are going to inherit salvation?
verses.2:1: Because of this, we must pay all the more attention to the things we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
verses.2:2: For if the word spoken through angels proved firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
verses.2:3: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation, which, having first begun to be spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,
verses.2:4: while God also testified alongside them both by signs and wonders and by various works of power and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to His will?
verses.2:5: For He did not subject to angels the inhabited world to come, about which we are speaking.
verses.2:6: But someone has testified somewhere, saying, "What is man, that You remember him, or a son of man, that You care for him?
verses.2:7: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor,
verses.2:8: You subjected all things beneath his feet." For in subjecting all things to him, He left nothing unsubjected to him. Yet at present we do not yet see all things subjected to him;
verses.2:9: but we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor on account of the suffering of death, so that by God's grace He might taste death on behalf of everyone.
verses.2:10: For it was fitting for Him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many sons to glory, to perfect the pioneer of their salvation through sufferings.
verses.2:11: For both He who sanctifies and those who are being sanctified are all from one; for this reason He is not ashamed to call them brothers,
verses.2:12: saying, "I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing praise to You";
verses.2:13: and again, "I will trust in Him"; and again, "Here I am, and the children whom God has given Me."
verses.2:14: Since then the children share in blood and flesh, He Himself likewise partook of the same things, so that through death He might bring to nothing the one who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,
verses.2:15: and release all those who through fear of death were subject to slavery throughout their entire life.
verses.2:16: For surely He does not help angels, but He helps the offspring of Abraham.
verses.2:17: Therefore He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in matters pertaining to God, in order to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
verses.2:18: For because He Himself has suffered when tested, He is able to come to the aid of those who are being tested.
verses.3:1: Therefore, holy brothers, sharers in a heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus,
verses.3:2: who was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses also was in His house.
verses.3:3: For He has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, by as much as the one who built the house has greater honor than the house itself.
verses.3:4: For every house is built by someone, but the One who built all things is God.
verses.3:5: Now Moses was faithful in all His house as a servant, for a testimony to the things that were to be spoken,
verses.3:6: but Christ was faithful as a Son over His house; whose house we are, if we hold fast our boldness and the boast of our hope.
verses.3:7: Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear His voice,
verses.3:8: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
verses.3:9: where your fathers put Me to the test in trial and saw My works
verses.3:10: for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, 'They always go astray in their heart, and they themselves have not known My ways,'
verses.3:11: as I swore in My wrath, 'They will never enter My rest.'"
verses.3:12: Watch out, brothers, so that there will never be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief in falling away from the living God;
verses.3:13: instead, exhort one another every day, as long as it is called "Today," so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
verses.3:14: For we have become sharers in Christ, if indeed we hold fast the beginning of our confidence firm until the end,
verses.3:15: while it is said, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."
verses.3:16: For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not indeed all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?
verses.3:17: And with whom was He indignant for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
verses.3:18: And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, except to those who disobeyed?
verses.3:19: And so we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.
verses.4:1: Therefore let us fear, while a promise remains of entering into His rest, that any one of you should seem to have fallen short.
verses.4:2: For indeed we have had good news proclaimed to us, just as they also did, but the word they heard did not benefit them, because they were not united by faith with those who heard.
verses.4:3: For we who have believed enter into rest, just as He has said, "As I swore in My wrath, 'They will never enter into My rest,'" even though the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
verses.4:4: For He has spoken somewhere concerning the seventh day in this way: "And God rested on the seventh day from all His works,"
verses.4:5: and in this passage again, "They will never enter into My rest."
verses.4:6: Therefore, since it remains for some to enter into it, and those who previously had good news proclaimed to them did not enter because of disobedience,
verses.4:7: He again appoints a certain day, "Today," saying through David after so long a time, just as has been said before: "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts."
verses.4:8: For if Joshua had given them rest, He would not have spoken about another day after those things.
verses.4:9: So then, there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
verses.4:10: For the one who has entered into His rest has himself also rested from his works, just as God did from His own.
verses.4:11: Therefore let us strive diligently to enter into that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.
verses.4:12: For the word of God is living and effective, and sharper than every two-edged sword, penetrating to the division of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and capable of judging the reflections and intentions of the heart.
verses.4:13: And no creature is unseen before Him, but all things are naked and laid bare to the eyes of Him to whom we must give an account.
verses.4:14: Therefore, having a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the confession.
verses.4:15: For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but One who has been tempted in all respects just like us, yet without sin.
verses.4:16: Therefore let us approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.
verses.5:1: For every high priest taken from among people is appointed on behalf of people in matters pertaining to God, so that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
verses.5:2: being able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, since he himself is also surrounded by weakness,
verses.5:3: and because of it he is obligated, just as for the people, so also for himself, to make offerings for sins.
verses.5:4: And no one takes the honor for himself, but only when called by God, just as Aaron also was.
verses.5:5: So also Christ did not glorify Himself to become a high priest, but He who spoke to Him did: "You are My Son; today I have fathered You,"
verses.5:6: just as He also says in another passage, "You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek."
verses.5:7: In the days of His flesh, having offered up both prayers and supplications with a loud cry and tears to the One able to save Him from death, and having been heard because of His reverence,
verses.5:8: although He was a Son, He learned obedience from the things He suffered;
verses.5:9: and having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him,
verses.5:10: having been designated by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.5:11: Concerning this we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, since you have become sluggish in hearing.
verses.5:12: For though because of the time you ought to be teachers, you again need someone to teach you the basic elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have come to need milk, not solid food.
verses.5:13: For everyone who partakes of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.
verses.5:14: But solid food is for the mature, for those who through practice have their faculties trained to distinguish both good and evil.
verses.6:1: Therefore, leaving behind the elementary teaching about Christ, let us move forward to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
verses.6:2: instruction about washings and the laying on of hands, and about the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
verses.6:3: And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
verses.6:4: For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
verses.6:5: and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the coming age,
verses.6:6: and have fallen away, to renew them again to repentance, since they crucify the Son of God again for themselves and expose Him to public disgrace.
verses.6:7: For ground that drinks the rain which often falls on it, and produces vegetation useful to those for whose sake it is also cultivated, receives a blessing from God;
verses.6:8: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near to a curse, and its end is burning.
verses.6:9: Yet concerning you, beloved, we are convinced of better things, things that accompany salvation, even though we speak in this way.
verses.6:10: For God is not unjust so as to forget your work and the love that you have shown toward His name, having served the saints and continuing to serve them.
verses.6:11: And we desire that each one of you show the same diligence toward the full assurance of hope until the end,
verses.6:12: so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
verses.6:13: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater by whom to swear, He swore by Himself,
verses.6:14: saying, "Surely, blessing I will bless you and multiplying I will multiply you."
verses.6:15: And thus, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
verses.6:16: For people swear by one greater than themselves, and for them an oath serves as confirmation, putting an end to every dispute.
verses.6:17: Accordingly, God, desiring all the more to demonstrate to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of His purpose, intervened with an oath,
verses.6:18: so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge may have strong encouragement to take hold of the hope set before us.
verses.6:19: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both secure and steadfast, and entering into the inner place behind the curtain,
verses.6:20: where Jesus entered as a forerunner on our behalf, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.7:1: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham as he returned from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
verses.7:2: to whom Abraham also apportioned a tenth of everything, first translated as king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace,
verses.7:3: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God, remains a priest continually.
verses.7:4: Now consider how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth from the choicest spoils.
verses.7:5: And those of the sons of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment to collect a tenth from the people according to the law, that is, from their brothers, even though they have come from the loins of Abraham.
verses.7:6: Yet the one whose genealogy is not from them received a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who held the promises.
verses.7:7: Now beyond any dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
verses.7:8: And here men who die receive tenths, but there one about whom it is testified that he lives.
verses.7:9: And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, who receives tenths, paid a tenth,
verses.7:10: for he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.
verses.7:11: Now if perfection were through the Levitical priesthood (for on the basis of it the people received the law), what further need would there be for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not be designated according to the order of Aaron?
verses.7:12: For when the priesthood is changed, of necessity a change of law also takes place.
verses.7:13: For He concerning whom these things are spoken belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
verses.7:14: For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe with reference to which Moses spoke nothing concerning priests.
verses.7:15: And it is even more abundantly clear if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
verses.7:16: who has become one not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life,
verses.7:17: for it is testified, "You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek."
verses.7:18: For on the one hand, a setting aside of a previous commandment takes place because of its weakness and uselessness
verses.7:19: (for the law made nothing perfect), and on the other hand, the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
verses.7:20: And inasmuch as it was not without an oath (for they indeed became priests without an oath,
verses.7:21: but He with an oath through the One who says to Him, "The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind, 'You are a priest forever'"),
verses.7:22: by so much also Jesus has become the guarantor of a better covenant.
verses.7:23: And those priests became many in number because they were prevented by death from continuing,
verses.7:24: but He, because He remains forever, holds His priesthood permanently.
verses.7:25: Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.
verses.7:26: For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and raised higher than the heavens,
verses.7:27: who does not have need daily, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people, for He did this once for all when He offered up Himself.
verses.7:28: For the law appoints men who have weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.
verses.8:1: Now the main point in what is being said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
verses.8:2: a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man.
verses.8:3: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary for this One also to have something to offer.
verses.8:4: Now if He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to the law;
verses.8:5: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was divinely warned when he was about to construct the tabernacle; for He says, "See that you make all things according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain."
verses.8:6: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as He is also the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted on better promises.
verses.8:7: For if that first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second.
verses.8:8: For finding fault with them, He says, "Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will conclude a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
verses.8:9: not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
verses.8:10: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws into their mind, and upon their hearts I will write them, and I will be God to them, and they will be a people to Me.
verses.8:11: And they will by no means teach each one his fellow citizen and each one his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for all will know Me, from the least to the greatest of them.
verses.8:12: For I will be merciful toward their unrighteous deeds, and their sins I will by no means remember any longer."
verses.8:13: In saying "new," He has made the first obsolete; and what is becoming obsolete and growing old is close to vanishing.
verses.9:1: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and the earthly sanctuary.
verses.9:2: For a tabernacle was prepared, the first one, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the bread; this is called the Holy Place.
verses.9:3: And behind the second curtain was a tabernacle called the Holy of Holies,
verses.9:4: having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which were a golden jar holding the manna, Aaron's staff that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant;
verses.9:5: and above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Concerning these things it is not now possible to speak in detail.
verses.9:6: Now when these things have been prepared in this way, the priests continually enter the first tabernacle, performing their acts of worship,
verses.9:7: but into the second only the high priest enters once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people.
verses.9:8: By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the sanctuary has not yet been disclosed while the first tabernacle still remains standing,
verses.9:9: which is a symbol for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot make the worshiper perfect in conscience,
verses.9:10: dealing only with foods and drinks and various washings, regulations of the flesh imposed until a time of reformation.
verses.9:11: But when Christ appeared as a high priest of the good things that have come, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is, not of this creation,
verses.9:12: and not through the blood of goats and calves, but through His own blood, He entered once for all into the sanctuary, having obtained eternal redemption.
verses.9:13: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the purification of the flesh,
verses.9:14: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without blemish to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
verses.9:15: And for this reason He is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
verses.9:16: For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established;
verses.9:17: for a will is confirmed upon death, since it is never in force while the one who made it is alive.
verses.9:18: Therefore not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.
verses.9:19: For when every commandment according to the law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
verses.9:20: saying, "This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you."
verses.9:21: And in the same way he sprinkled both the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry with the blood.
verses.9:22: And according to the law nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
verses.9:23: Therefore it was necessary for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
verses.9:24: For Christ did not enter a sanctuary made with hands, a counterpart of the true one, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf;
verses.9:25: nor was it so that He would offer Himself repeatedly, just as the high priest enters the sanctuary year by year with blood not his own,
verses.9:26: otherwise He would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world; but now once at the consummation of the ages He has been manifested to do away with sin through His sacrifice.
verses.9:27: And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after this comes judgment,
verses.9:28: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those who eagerly await Him, for salvation.
verses.10:1: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the image itself of the realities, can never, by the same sacrifices that they offer continually year by year, perfect those who draw near.
verses.10:2: Otherwise, would they not have ceased being offered, since the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
verses.10:3: Instead, in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
verses.10:4: for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to remove sins.
verses.10:5: Therefore, when entering the world, He says, "Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me;
verses.10:6: in whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You were not pleased.
verses.10:7: Then I said, 'Look, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written about Me) to do Your will, God.'"
verses.10:8: Saying above, "Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You did not desire, nor were You pleased with them" (which are offered according to the law),
verses.10:9: then He has said, "Look, I have come to do Your will." He removes the first so that He may establish the second.
verses.10:10: By that will, we have been sanctified through the offering of Jesus Christ's body once for all.
verses.10:11: And every priest stands day by day ministering and repeatedly offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
verses.10:12: He, however, after offering a single sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
verses.10:13: waiting from that time onward until His enemies are placed as a footstool for His feet.
verses.10:14: For with one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
verses.10:15: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
verses.10:16: "This is the covenant that I will establish with them after those days," says the Lord: "I will put My laws upon their hearts, and upon their minds I will write them,"
verses.10:17: and, "Their sins and their lawless deeds I will never again remember."
verses.10:18: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.
verses.10:19: Therefore, brothers, having confidence for entrance into the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,
verses.10:20: which He inaugurated for us as a new and living way through the curtain, that is, His flesh,
verses.10:21: and having a great priest over the house of God,
verses.10:22: let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
verses.10:23: Let us hold firmly to the confession of our hope unwaveringly, for He who promised is faithful;
verses.10:24: and let us consider one another in order to spur on love and good works,
verses.10:25: not abandoning our own gathering together, as is the custom of some, but encouraging one another, and so much the more as you see the day approaching.
verses.10:26: For if we continue sinning deliberately after having received the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains any longer,
verses.10:27: but a certain terrifying expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that is about to devour the adversaries.
verses.10:28: Anyone who has rejected the law of Moses dies without mercy on the basis of two or three witnesses.
verses.10:29: How much worse a punishment do you suppose he will be counted worthy of who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and regarded the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified as common, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
verses.10:30: For we know the One who said, "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay." And again, "The Lord will judge His people."
verses.10:31: It is terrifying to fall into the hands of the living God.
verses.10:32: But recall the earlier days, in which, after being enlightened, you endured a great struggle of sufferings,
verses.10:33: partly being made a spectacle through both reproaches and afflictions, and partly becoming companions of those who were treated this way.
verses.10:34: For you both sympathized with the prisoners and accepted with joy the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you yourselves have a better and abiding possession.
verses.10:35: Therefore, do not cast aside your confidence, which holds a great reward;
verses.10:36: for you need endurance, so that after doing the will of God you may receive the promise.
verses.10:37: For, "Yet a very little while, the One who is coming will come and will not delay;
verses.10:38: but My righteous one will live by faith, and if he shrinks back, My soul is not pleased with him."
verses.10:39: We, however, are not among those who shrink back to destruction, but among those who have faith for the preservation of the soul.
verses.11:1: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the proof of realities not seen.
verses.11:2: For by it the elders were attested.
verses.11:3: By faith we understand that the ages have been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not come into being from things that appear.
verses.11:4: By faith Abel offered to God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he was attested to be righteous, with God testifying concerning his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks.
verses.11:5: By faith Enoch was transferred so as not to see death, and he was not found because God transferred him; for before his transfer he had been attested to have pleased God.
verses.11:6: And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for the one approaching God must believe that He exists and that He becomes a rewarder to those who earnestly seek Him.
verses.11:7: By faith Noah, having been divinely warned about things not yet seen, in reverence constructed an ark for the salvation of his household, through which he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that is according to faith.
verses.11:8: By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed to go out to a place that he was about to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
verses.11:9: By faith he resided as a foreigner in the land of the promise, as in a land not his own, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the co-heirs of the same promise;
verses.11:10: for he was waiting for the city that has the foundations, whose designer and maker is God.
verses.11:11: By faith, together with Sarah herself, he received power for the depositing of seed even past the proper time of age, since he considered the One who promised to be faithful.
verses.11:12: Therefore also from one man, and him as good as dead, there were born as many as the stars of heaven in multitude, and as the innumerable sand along the shore of the sea.
verses.11:13: All these died according to faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them from afar and greeted them, and having confessed that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.
verses.11:14: For those who say such things make it plain that they are seeking a homeland.
verses.11:15: And indeed, if they were keeping in mind that land from which they went out, they would have had an opportunity to return;
verses.11:16: but as it is, they long for a better one, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for He prepared a city for them.
verses.11:17: By faith Abraham, when being tested, offered up Isaac; and the one who had received the promises was offering up his one and only son,
verses.11:18: to whom it was spoken, "In Isaac seed will be named for you,"
verses.11:19: having reasoned that God is able even to raise from the dead; from which also he received him back in a figure.
verses.11:20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.
verses.11:21: By faith Jacob, while dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshiped upon the top of his staff.
verses.11:22: By faith Joseph, nearing his end, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions concerning his bones.
verses.11:23: By faith Moses, after being born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the decree of the king.
verses.11:24: By faith Moses, having grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
verses.11:25: choosing rather to be mistreated together with the people of God than to have the temporary enjoyment of sin,
verses.11:26: considering the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt; for he was looking toward the reward.
verses.11:27: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he persevered as seeing the invisible One.
verses.11:28: By faith he observed the Passover and the pouring out of the blood, so that the one destroying the firstborn would not touch them.
verses.11:29: By faith they crossed through the Red Sea as through dry land; when the Egyptians made an attempt on it, they were swallowed up.
verses.11:30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after having been encircled for seven days.
verses.11:31: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish together with those who were disobedient, having welcomed the spies with peace.
verses.11:32: And what more should I say? For time will fail me if I tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel, and the prophets,
verses.11:33: who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
verses.11:34: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edges of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.
verses.11:35: Women received back their dead by resurrection; and others were tortured, not accepting release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
verses.11:36: And still others experienced mockings and scourgings, and furthermore chains and imprisonment.
verses.11:37: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were tested, they died by slaughter of the sword; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, mistreated
verses.11:38: —of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and the holes of the earth.
verses.11:39: And all these, though having been attested through faith, did not receive the promise,
verses.11:40: since God had provided something better concerning us, so that apart from us they would not be made perfect.
verses.12:1: Therefore, since we also have so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, laying aside every weight and the sin that closely clings, let us run with endurance the race set before us,
verses.12:2: looking intently to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before Him endured a cross, despising shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.12:3: For consider carefully Him who has endured such hostility from sinners against themselves, so that you may not grow weary in your souls, losing heart.
verses.12:4: You have not yet resisted to the point of blood, struggling against sin,
verses.12:5: and you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: "My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor lose heart when reproved by Him;
verses.12:6: for the one whom the Lord loves He disciplines, and He scourges every son whom He receives."
verses.12:7: Endure for the sake of discipline; God deals with you as with sons. For what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
verses.12:8: But if you are without discipline, of which all have become sharers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
verses.12:9: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh as those who disciplined us, and we respected them; will we not much rather be subject to the Father of spirits and live?
verses.12:10: For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed best to them, but He does so for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness.
verses.12:11: Now all discipline for the present does not seem to be a matter of joy, but of sorrow; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
verses.12:12: Therefore straighten up the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
verses.12:13: and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
verses.12:14: Pursue peace with everyone, and the sanctification without which no one will see the Lord,
verses.12:15: watching carefully so that no one falls short of the grace of God, so that no root of bitterness springing up causes trouble and through it many become defiled,
verses.12:16: so that there be no sexually immoral or godless person like Esau, who in exchange for a single meal sold his own birthright.
verses.12:17: For you know that afterward, even when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, though he earnestly sought it with tears.
verses.12:18: For you have not come to what can be touched, and to a blazing fire, and darkness, and gloom, and a tempest,
verses.12:19: and to the blast of a trumpet and a voice of words, whose hearers begged that no further word be added to them;
verses.12:20: for they could not bear what was being commanded: "Even if a wild beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned."
verses.12:21: And—so terrifying was the sight—Moses said, "I am terrified and trembling."
verses.12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels, in festal gathering,
verses.12:23: and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the Judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
verses.12:24: and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better than Abel.
verses.12:25: See that you do not refuse the One who is speaking. For if those did not escape when they refused the One who warned them on earth, much less will we escape if we turn away from the One from heaven,
verses.12:26: whose voice shook the earth then, but now He has promised, saying, "Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heaven."
verses.12:27: Now the phrase "Yet once more" indicates the removal of the things being shaken, as of things that have been made, so that the things not being shaken may remain.
verses.12:28: Therefore, receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us show gratitude, through which we may worship God acceptably with reverence and awe;
verses.12:29: for indeed our God is a consuming fire.
verses.13:2: Do not forget hospitality, for through this some have unknowingly hosted angels.
verses.13:3: Remember the prisoners, as though bound with them, and those being mistreated, since you yourselves are also in the body.
verses.13:4: Let marriage be honored among all, and the marriage bed be undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
verses.13:5: Let your way of life be free from the love of money, being content with what you have; for He Himself has said, "I will never leave you, nor will I ever abandon you,"
verses.13:6: so that we say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper, and I will not be afraid. What will man do to me?"
verses.13:7: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; closely observing the outcome of their way of life, imitate their faith.
verses.13:8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and for eternity.
verses.13:9: Do not be carried away by diverse and strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, in which those who walk have not been benefited.
verses.13:10: We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle have no authority to eat.
verses.13:11: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin are burned up outside the camp.
verses.13:12: For this reason Jesus also, so that He might sanctify the people through His own blood, suffered outside the gate.
verses.13:13: So then, let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.
verses.13:14: For we do not have an enduring city here, but we are seeking the one to come.
verses.13:15: Through Him, therefore, let us offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips confessing His name.
verses.13:16: And do not forget doing good and sharing, for God is well pleased with such sacrifices.
verses.13:17: Obey your leaders and yield to them, for they keep watch over your souls as ones who will give an account, so that they may do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would be unprofitable for you.
verses.13:18: Pray for us, for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, desiring to conduct ourselves honorably in all things.
verses.13:19: And I urge you even more to do this, so that I may be restored to you sooner.
verses.13:20: Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep by the blood of an eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
verses.13:21: equip you in every good thing for doing His will, working in us what is well-pleasing before Him through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.13:22: Now I urge you, brothers, bear with the word of exhortation, for indeed I have written to you in few words.
verses.13:23: Know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom I will see you if he comes soon.
verses.13:24: Greet all your leaders and all the saints; those from Italy send you greetings.
verses.13:25: May grace be with all of you.

notes.1:2: Greek τοὺς αἰῶνας literally means "the ages," used here (as in 11:3) for the created order of time and space.
notes.1:6: Greek πάλιν ("again") stands inside the temporal clause ("when He again brings"), though some take it with the main verb ("And again, when He brings").
notes.1:7: Greek πνεύματα can mean either "winds" (matching the Hebrew of Psalm 104:4) or "spirits" (anticipating "ministering spirits" in 1:14).
notes.1:8: Greek ὁ θεός is translated as a vocative ("O God") addressing the Son, though grammatically it can also be read as a predicate nominative ("God is Your throne"). The critical text reads αὐτοῦ ("His kingdom") rather than σου ("Your kingdom").
notes.2:7: Greek βραχύ τι ("a little") can express either degree ("a little lower," as in Psalm 8:5) or duration ("for a little while"); the same phrase recurs in 2:9.
notes.2:10: Greek ἀρχηγόν ("pioneer") denotes a founder, originator, or trailblazing leader who opens the way for others.
notes.2:11: Greek ἐξ ἑνός ("from one") is deliberately concise and may refer to one Father (God) or one common origin.
notes.2:16: Greek ἐπιλαμβάνεται literally means "takes hold of," used here in the sense of coming to someone's aid; σπέρματος literally means "seed" or "offspring."
notes.3:2: Greek τῷ ποιήσαντι αὐτόν literally means "the One who made Him," an idiom for appointing someone to an office (cf. 1 Samuel 12:6 LXX; Mark 3:14).
notes.3:9: The critical text reads ἐπείρασαν ... ἐν δοκιμασίᾳ ("put [Me] to the test in trial"), without an explicit pronoun "Me," rather than the later variant "tested Me and proved Me."
notes.3:11: Greek Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται literally reads "If they will enter," reflecting a Hebrew oath formula that expresses an emphatic negation ("They will never enter").
notes.3:14: Greek ὑπόστασις here denotes firm "confidence" or "assurance," contrasting with its sense of "essence" or "essential being" in 1:3.
notes.4:2: The Greek text reads the accusative plural participle sygkekerasmenous ("not united by faith with those who heard"), referring to the unbelieving Israelites; a textual variant reads the nominative singular, meaning "the word was not united with faith in those who heard."
notes.4:3: The Greek oath formula ei eiseleusontai (literally "if they will enter") reflects the Hebrew emphatic negative oath idiom, "They will never enter."
notes.4:8: Greek Iesous is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, referring here to Joshua son of Nun who led Israel into Canaan.
notes.4:13: Greek tetrachelismena ("laid bare") literally refers to bending back the neck so as to expose the throat; logos at the end of the verse means "account," forming a wordplay with logos ("word") in 4:12.
notes.5:7: The phrase apo tes eulabeias is debated: it most likely means "because of His reverence (or godly submission)," though some understand it as "saved from fear (or dread)."
notes.5:8: The Greek features a well-known wordplay between emathen ("learned") and epathen ("suffered").
notes.5:11: Greek Peri hou may be taken as neuter ("Concerning this," referring to the subject of Christ's priesthood) or masculine ("Concerning him," referring to Melchizedek).
notes.6:2: The Greek text reads the accusative didachen ("instruction") in apposition to "foundation" in 6:1, while some manuscripts read the genitive didaches. Plural baptismon typically denotes ceremonial washings rather than exclusively Christian baptism.
notes.6:6: Greek anastaurountas can mean either "crucifying again" or simply "crucifying," and its force may be causal ("since") or temporal ("while").
notes.6:14: Greek Ei men ("Surely") with the cognate participles ("blessing I will bless... multiplying I will multiply") preserves the Septuagint rendering of the emphatic Hebrew infinitive absolute in Genesis 22:17.
notes.6:17: Greek emesiteusen literally means "intervened" or "acted as mediator," expressing how God guaranteed His promise by interposing an oath.
notes.7:21: The Greek text here follows the shorter reading, omitting "according to the order of Melchizedek" found in later manuscripts.
notes.7:24: The Greek adjective ἀπαράβατος ("permanently") can mean either "unchanging" or "non-transferable," indicating a priesthood that does not pass to a successor.
notes.7:25: The phrase εἰς τὸ παντελές ("completely") can express both completeness ("utterly") and duration ("for all time").
notes.8:8: The dative pronoun αὐτοῖς may be construed either with "finding fault" ("finding fault with them") or with "He says" ("finding fault, He says to them").
notes.8:12: The Greek text follows the shorter reading, omitting "and their lawless deeds" found in some manuscripts.
notes.9:4: The Greek term θυμιατήριον can refer either to the golden altar of incense or to a portable golden censer used on the Day of Atonement.
notes.9:11: The Greek text reads γενομένων ("that have come") rather than the variant μελλόντων ("to come").
notes.9:14: The Greek text reads ὑμῶν ("your conscience") rather than ἡμῶν ("our conscience"); "through the eternal Spirit" (διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου) may refer either to the Holy Spirit or to Christ's own eternal spiritual nature.
notes.9:16: In verses 16-17, the Greek noun διαθήκη ("covenant") shifts to its legal sense of "will" or "testament," playing on the dual meaning of the term.
notes.10:5: "A body You prepared for Me" follows the Septuagint of Psalm 40:6 (LXX 39:7), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "ears You have dug [or opened] for Me."
notes.10:12: The Greek phrase "for all time" (εἰς τὸ διηνεκές) stands between "sacrifice" and "sat down" and may modify either—"offered one sacrifice for sins for all time" or "sat down for all time."
notes.10:17: The Greek sentence begun in v. 15 ("for after saying...") is elliptical, leaving the resumed verb of speaking (e.g., "He then adds") unexpressed before this clause.
notes.10:34: The critical Greek text reads "the prisoners" (τοῖς δεσμίοις) and "you yourselves" (ἑαυτούς); some later manuscripts read "my chains" and add "in heaven."
notes.11:1: Greek hypostasis can mean "assurance," "reality," or "foundation," while elenchos denotes "proof" or "conviction."
notes.11:11: The Greek text reads the dative aute Sarra ("with Sarah herself"), making Abraham the subject of "received power" and katabolen spermatos ("depositing of seed") a reference to fathering offspring; other manuscripts read the nominative, making Sarah the subject.
notes.11:21: Follows the Septuagint of Gen 47:31, which vocalized the Hebrew consonantal text as "staff" (matteh) rather than "bed" (mittah).
notes.11:37: The Greek text includes epeirasthesan ("they were tested") after "they were sawn in two," a word omitted in several early manuscripts.
notes.12:1: Greek euperistatos appears only here in the New Testament and may mean "closely clinging," "easily entangling," or "readily surrounding."
notes.12:2: Greek anti here may mean "for (the sake of)" the joy set before Him or "instead of" a joy He gave up.
notes.12:3: The Greek text reads the plural reflexive eis heautous ("against themselves," indicating hostility that harms the sinners themselves); other manuscripts read the singular "against Himself."
notes.12:22: Greek panegyrei ("festal gathering") may stand in apposition to "myriads of angels" here or be grouped with "assembly of the firstborn" in v. 23.
notes.12:28: The Greek idiom echomen charin normally means "let us show gratitude," though some understand it as "let us hold fast to grace."
notes.13:4: The opening clauses are verbless in Greek and may be read either as an exhortation ("Let marriage be honored...") or as an indicative statement ("Marriage is honorable..."); similarly, "among all" (en pasin) can also be rendered "in every respect."
notes.13:21: Some manuscripts read "working in you" (hymin) instead of "working in us" (hemin), and some omit "and ever" (ton aionon); the translation follows the critical text.
notes.13:24: The phrase "those from Italy" (hoi apo tes Italias) may refer either to believers in Italy sending greetings outward or to Italian believers currently with the author sending greetings back to Italy.
